title: Oncall Scene Protocol and Event Normalization
content:
Purpose:
This is a field-oriented oncall protocol for first responders and incident leads focused on: 1) consistent evidence capture when RBAC-v2 events are involved, 2) minimal-impact scene handling for production services, and 3) deterministic event normalization for SIEM export and downstream postmortems.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to security oncall (PagerDuty: sec-oncall) and L1 SREs responding to access anomalies, privilege escalations, or audit-log drift tied to RBAC-v2.
- Assumes access to the security runbook Slack channel, read-only access to the audit log stream, and ability to request temporary elevated access per emergency SOP.
- This is NOT the decision-maker escalation policy; use the escalation matrix when containment or customer impact crosses threshold.

Quick triage (first 15 minutes):
1) Identify signal: alert name, source system, rule that fired (e.g., rbac-unauthorized-api-call, audit-ingest-failure).
2) Snapshot: capture incident id, alert window, top 3 affected principals (user/service account/role), and the last successful audit-log watermark.
3) Stabilize comms: create Slack incident thread and add sec-oncall, oncall-sre, and product-eng for affected service. Note the timezone of the primary oncall.
4) Non-disruptive containment: if unknown account is present, rotate short-lived credentials tied to that account and block new tokens using routing policy. DO NOT mass-revoke org-wide keys unless instructed by incident lead.

On-scene evidence capture checklist (minimal required fields):
- incident_id: internal id (sec-YYYYMMDD-XXXXX)
- time_observed_utc: ISO8601 timestamp of first alert
- alert_source: service name (e.g., audit-ingest, rbac-service, gateway)
- raw_event_ids: list of native event ids (audit.log.id, kafka offset, cloudtrail id) -- capture as CSV if multiple
- principal_type: user | service_account | role
- principal_identifier: e.g., email, service account id
- action: API/method invoked, route, CLI command
- resource_identifier: model/version/cluster/route
- ip_and_region: observed IPs and geo if available
- auth_path: token type and grant (e.g., oauth, k8s-sa, api-key)
- pre_containment_state: what access existed before any mitigation
- initial_hypothesis: short sentence

Notes on RBAC-v2 specific captures:
- Always capture the RBAC change delta (if any) that precedes the event: policy_id, rule_id, actor, timestamp, diff (allow -> deny or vice versa).
- If the event is about role assumption or temporary elevation, include the policy_bindings array (comma-separated) that shows which groups/principals were granted the binding and whether binding was time-limited.
- When possible, capture the evaluated policy trace (policy engine decision path or trace id) so that post-incident review can reconstruct why the decision was allowed/denied.

Event normalization for SIEM export (required fields and mapping guidance):
Goal: make a deterministic, searchable record that downstream SOC analysts and automated correlation rules can depend on. Normalize as soon as possible (during evidence-harvest or ingestion).
- normal.event_id = incident_id
- normal.timestamp = time_observed_utc
- normal.source = alert_source
- normal.actor.type = principal_type
- normal.actor.id = principal_identifier
- normal.actor.roles = policy_bindings (flatten CSV)
- normal.action = action
- normal.resource = resource_identifier
- normal.network.ip = ip_and_region
- normal.auth.method = auth_path
- normal.rbac.change = policy_delta_summary
- normal.raw_refs = raw_event_ids

Normalization rules (practical tips):
- Flatten arrays to CSV fields for legacy SIEM compatibility; add a full-json_ref pointer to archived evidence for teams that can parse JSON blobs.
- Standardize time to UTC ISO8601 with millisecond precision. If exact ms not available, use the ingest timestamp plus note "approximate".
- Map internal service names to canonical service keys before export (example mapping table maintained in Confluence link).

Handoff checklist (when transferring incident to another shift or team):
- Update incident channel header with: incident_id, short status (triaged / contained / mitigated / escalated), blocking items.
- Attach normalized SIEM packet (normal.* fields above) into the incident doc.
- Share the last 3 raw event ids and where the raw can be retrieved (s3 path, ELK URL, Kafka offsets).
- Record any temporary mitigations and TTLs (rotations, ACLs, firewall blocks).
- If access was escalated, include who approved, approval ticket id, and revocation ETA.
- Items for follow-up: evidence integrity checks, deeper forensics, external disclosure, legal involvement. Assign an owner for each.

Containment decision matrix (high level):
- If active exploitation or data exfiltration suspected -> immediate containment: isolate affected service, strip network egress, rotate affected credentials, notify customer-success if customer-visible. Escalate to incident commander.
- If no active exploitation and blast radius limited -> targeted mitigations (revoke specific bindings, patch role misconfig). Document rollback plan before changing policy.
- If unclear -> gather evidence for 30–60 minutes, prioritize obtaining policy-engine trace and raw audit slices, then decide.

Preservation & evidence automation pointers:
- Trigger the evidence-harvest lambda: payload must include raw_event_ids, incident_id, s3-destination prefix, and a harvest_ttl label.
- If harvest fails, snapshot the log stream offsets and mark the incident ticket with the offsets to prevent log rotation gaps.
- Tag harvested evidence with: incident_id, collected_by (oncall), collection_time_utc, and manifest_checksum.

SIEM export edge cases and validation checks before export:
- Validate actor id normalization: drop ephemeral session ids in actor.id and prefer stable principal id where possible.
- If policy_bindings are >200 items, export a summary token (count + top-5 principals) and archive full list in evidence store with pointer.
- When policy_delta_summary contains binary blobs or encoded config, store as artifact not inline. SIEM fields should be readable text.

Post-incident notes template (to be appended to incident doc during postmortem):
- Summary: 2–3 sentence overview of what happened and impact.
- Root cause hypothesis: concise statement and evidence pointers.
- Timeline: key events with normalized timestamps (UTC).
- Detection: which rule alerted and why did it fire at that time.
- Containment & remediation actions: what changed and why.
- Evidence inventory: list of harvested artifacts (s3 paths, archive ids) and locations.
- RBAC changes required: short steps to remediate policy or guardrail gaps.
- Lessons & follow-ups: guardrail owners, CI tests to add, metric thresholds to tune.

Speed notes and common pitfalls (learned from prior incidents):
- Pitfall: mass policy rollbacks to "fix" an incident — often introduces noisy alerts. Prefer targeted revocation and a clear rollback plan.
- Pitfall: exporting raw tokens to the SIEM field; do not include secrets. Mask or truncate sensitive fields before export.
- Pitfall: delayed harvesting until after containment — log rotation often loses context. Harvest early.

Quick templates (copy into incident doc):
- Incident header line: [incident_id] [severity] [short description] [status]
- Evidence capture line: incident_id, time_observed_utc, alert_source, principal_identifier, action, resource_identifier, raw_event_ids
- Handoff line: owner -> next_owner | block_items: x,y,z | evidence_prefix: s3://sec-evidence/incident_id/

Appendix: minimal field glossary (for oncall readability):
- policy_bindings: the list of groups/roles attached to the principal at the time of the event (flattened).
- policy_delta_summary: human readable summary of a policy change (who changed what, from->to).
- evaluated_policy_trace: a trace id you can query from the policy engine to see decision steps.
- raw_event_ids: native ids to pull original logs.

Open items before finalization:
- Confirm canonical service name mapping table is published and versioned; avoid freeform service names in normalized export. (Owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-01-05)
- Add automated mask for api-keys in exported fields (Owner: Asha Kapoor, due: 2026-02-01)
- Define retention policy for harvested evidence beyond current 90 days for high-severity incidents (Legal input needed).

If you are the oncall taking this: read the oncall playbook cover page, follow the quick triage checklist, capture the minimal evidence fields, start the evidence-harvest automation, and escalate using the matrix if anything looks like active exploitation. Document everything in the incident channel — small notes saved often are more valuable than large reconstructions.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-20: initial draft (Priya Shah)
- 2025-12-10: added RBAC-v2 capture fields and normalization mapping (Diego Morales)
- 2026-01-15: added containment decision matrix and harvest automation steps (Asha Kapoor)
- 2026-02-14: editorial pass and open items added (Priya Shah)

End of document.
